findings.finding: Q-COND-1(a) places the one-writer holds test inside the condition conjunction, which makes the pressure machine unreachable. Q-COND-0 (§3): 'eligible = { r ∈ rows : C1 ∧ C2 ∧ … ∧ C11 }'; Q-COND-1(a): 'r.holds ∩ inprog_holds = ∅ — the one-writer invariant, always'; §8 step 5: 'eligible = rows satisfying Q-COND-1..11'. If a conflict-blocked row fails C1(a), it is not eligible, so 'the top eligible row is conflict-blocked' (R5, Q-CAP-1) can never occur — there is no 'blocked next', no anchor, no drops, no cap-drop, and the entire 'aging the operator remembers' (§1.2, §2.2) is inert. The spec contradicts itself in the same breath: Q-ORD-7 requires the anchor to be 'still eligible and still conflict-blocked' (eligible ∧ blocked is the empty set under C1(a)); Q-CAP-3's own exclusion list ('excluded from eligible by needs, appetite, backoff, heal cooldown, host-quiet, missing bundle, missing acceptance, or pending ratification') omits holds-conflict, i.e. the anchor definition assumes holds-conflict does NOT exclude; Q-ORD-4's 'including rows that were eligible but conflict-blocked' accrual clause is vacuous under the same reading. The recovered code keeps the two holds tests in the §8 step-9 candidate filter, not in `elig` (tools/fleet-keeper.sh:770-781, verified: `candidates = []` at :770, first test 'if e["holds"] & inprog_holds: continue' at :772, second at :774, `pick = candidates[0]` at :781), precisely so a blocked row stays eligible and anchors.
findings.disposition: RESOLVE BEFORE BUILD. Move Q-COND-1(a) and (b) out of the §3 condition conjunction into the §8 step-9 candidate filter (where the recovered code and the H2/H3 controls already place them); keep only Q-COND-1(c) (held-children exclusion, pass-2 §2.1) as a condition. Restate Q-COND-0's shape as 'eligible = rows satisfying C2..C11 plus C1(c); the C1(a)/(b) holds tests are evaluated at step 9'. Controls H1-H3 then test the dispatch decision as intended; the anchor can form again.

findings.finding: S03 §4 (appetite) is written against a model that pass-2 rev-2 has replaced, on a named touch point. S03 Q-COND-3: 'appetite permits — §4 in full', and S03 §4 specifies the five static levels (OFF < PROBE < CONSERVE < SPEND < RESERVED, from measurement-methodology.md §1) with mechanism mappings (Q-APP-2 hard OFF via model_allowed; Q-APP-4 CONSERVE sub-cap 1 + lane substitution + window guard; Q-APP-3 RESERVED reserved_for). Pass-2 rev-2 §4.1 says 'The static levels OFF < PROBE < CONSERVE < SPEND < RESERVED (measurement-methodology.md:23) are replaced by a continuous integer dial per family' with appetite(f) ∈ {0..99}, lanes(f) and spacing(f) (§4.2), and §4.5 migrates the levels away ('superseded rather than orphaned'). S03 was authored against pass-2 rev-1 (its §0/§10 cite 'pass 2 §8.2', a rev-1 number — see N12) and never synced to rev-2. Pass-2 §4.2 explicitly defers ordering to S03 ('The dial must not perturb the eligibility ordering — ordering is S03's concern', citing S03 §2.1) but nothing in S03 defers appetite to the dial. As written, the supervisor will implement the dial (pass-2 §4 is a Must, pass-2 §10.2 never-cut) and Q-COND-3 will evaluate appetite against a mechanism that does not exist.
findings.disposition: RESOLVE BEFORE BUILD. Either (a) rewrite S03 §4 (Q-APP-1..8, §4's controls A1-A8) against the pass-2 rev-2 dial — appetite(f) 0-99, lanes(f)/spacing(f), the reservation predicate as a separate hard gate, the operator/supervisor write hierarchy — and re-map the A-arms, or (b) rule the dial out explicitly and ratify the levels as the queue's appetite. Option (a) is the coherent one: pass-2 §4.5's migration and S03's Q-APP-7 (reservations outrank appetite) agree in spirit, and pass-2's reduce-only rule (§4.4) is compatible with S03's Q-APP-1 axis rule. The two documents cannot both ship as written.

findings.finding: Q-ORD-7's stated rationale is mechanically impossible. The clause says: 'two starved mutation rows accrue in lockstep and can swap places, and every swap is a re-anchor that resets drops = 0 (:694-698), so c_eff never falls and the pressure machine becomes vacuous'. Under the spec's own keys (Q-ORD-3: effective desc, then age desc, then added asc), two rows accruing in lockstep have EQUAL age forever, so they can never swap on key 3, and key 4 (added asc) orders them permanently — the older row always runs first. Same-priority lockstep rows: zero swaps. Different-priority lockstep rows: exactly one swap, at the saturation boundary (when both effective values hit the 99 cap, key 3 ties on equal age and key 4 FIFO takes over), then stable. Repeated churn — the case stickiness exists to stop — requires differential accrual (one row ineligible for some fires, so its age falls behind) or a re-joining higher-priority row. The stickiness clause itself is still justified (differential-accrual churn is real and re-anchors would reset drops), but the named mechanism is wrong, and arm P4 as written ('a second row's effective overtakes it') does not state which overtake mechanism the seed uses.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Rewrite the Q-ORD-7 'Why this clause exists' paragraph to name the real churn drivers: (i) a row that missed accrual (ineligibility window) rejoining below a saturated competitor, and (ii) a higher-priority row entering or re-entering the eligible set while the anchor is blocked. Re-key arm P4's seed to one of those two (e.g., the anchor at priority 50 age 45 (effective 95), a second row priority 60 that was ineligible for 5 fires entering at age 40 with effective 99 — it overtakes on effective, and the arm asserts anchor/drops persist).

findings.finding: Q-ORD-6's crossover claim ('A default row (50) overtakes a pinned 99 after 49 fires it loses') and arm O3 ('overtakes at exactly fire 49, not 48, not 50') are not guaranteed under the spec's own accrual rule. Q-ORD-4 accrues +1 to every eligible row not fired, 'including rows that were eligible but conflict-blocked'. A pinned 99 that is eligible (which is the natural reading of 'pinned' — the operator's 'a blocked task's priority climbs each block') accrues in lockstep with the default row: at fire 49 both have age 49, effective 99, equal age, and key 4 (added asc) decides — the earlier-entered row wins, so a later-entering default NEVER overtakes an earlier-added pinned 99. The crossover only materializes if the pinned row accrues nothing (ineligible for those fires, e.g. model denied or backoff) or if the default entered first. O3 does not seed either condition, so its asserted outcome is not guaranteed. Consequence for Open question 2: AGE_CAP 48 vs 49 is nearly moot — a pinned 99 is effectively absolute against later-entering defaults either way (the tie falls to FIFO, not to the starved row); the only real overtake path is a pinned row that misses accrual. The spec's mental model of its own saturation ('reachable ties, resolved by age, in the starved row's favour') overstates key 3's reach.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Pin O3's seed: the base-99 row must be excluded from the eligible set for all 49 fires (or the base-50 row must be the earlier entrant) for the asserted outcome to hold. Restate Q-ORD-6's crossover and OQ2's analysis to say that under lockstep accrual a pinned 99 ties at saturation and FIFO decides — the starved row's age only wins when it accrued strictly more fires (an ineligibility window), which is exactly the differential-accrual case of N3.

findings.finding: Q-NIGHT-5's classification has no branch for a child that never declares `step`, which every legacy worker is. Q-NIGHT-4 promises backward compatibility: 'a legacy bare [progress] line still satisfies liveness — it just yields no ETA', and arm NG4 asserts 'legacy bare [progress] ⇒ liveness satisfied, ETA-UNKNOWN reported (not blank)'. But Q-NIGHT-5 classifies by three observables including `step`: ADVANCING requires 'step strictly increased since the previous classification'; BEATING-STALLED requires 'step unchanged for ≥ STALL_S'. A legacy child has no step at all: 'strictly increased' is false (null), 'unchanged' is trivially true (null never changes) — so every legacy child is classified BEATING-STALLED forever, i.e. permanently a 'zombie-suspect — alive, reporting, not advancing'. Every legacy worker would be reported as a zombie-suspect every poll, the same false-alarm-that-trains-readers-to-ignore-it shape the spec itself cites in the logjam-flag lifecycle (T514 comment, fleet-keeper.sh:748-762) and in pass-2's F5. ETA already has its own no-declaration branch (ETA-UNKNOWN); the class needs the same.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Add a fifth class (e.g. UNDECLARED-STEP: heartbeat fresh, no step ever declared — alive and reporting, ETA-UNKNOWN, not a zombie-suspect) or make BEATING-STALLED require a previously-declared step (legacy children classified by heartbeat-only, equivalent to ADVANCING-without-ETA). State what happens to the class when a brief is later upgraded to the step=i/n contract (the class should switch to ADVANCING on the first declared step).

findings.finding: S03 §7 (Q-MINT-1..10) and pass-2 rev-2 §5 (RUN-1..5) are two independent re-specs of the same operator ruling (§7.5 of the orchestration sketch) that disagree on field shapes and mechanisms. Differences: minted_by is 'the parent task id' in Q-MINT-1 vs '{task_id, model, supervisor_pid}' in pass-2 RUN-2; the uniqueness key is sha256(title‖deliverables‖acceptance) with a --supersedes override in Q-MINT-5 vs '(holds, justification-key)' in pass-2 RUN-4 (and 'justification-key' is itself undefined — T574 N3); depth is MINT_DEPTH_MAX=3 with an auto-admit boundary at depth ≤ 1 (Q-MINT-3) vs pass-2's operator-set D_max with no auto-admit rule; S03 adds pending-ratification as a store status (§11) and Q-MINT-6/7/8 (disjoint deliverables, decreases measure, runnability-at-mint) have no pass-2 counterpart, while pass-2's RUN-1 mint-delta circuit breaker has no S03 counterpart. Both are Must-level. A build following both must silently choose; nothing reconciles them. The two documents do not even agree on the meaning of 'justification' vs 'mint_justification' in the store schema (S03 §11).
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Merge into one regime: pass-2 §5 owns the write-time enforcement and the delta circuit breaker; S03 §7 owns the ordering/quarantine/ratification policy (pending-ratification status, depth/fan-out/tree/rate caps, supersedes). Pin one field set (minted_by as an identity record per RUN-2, justification per RUN-3) and delete the duplicate from the other document. The operator's §7.5 requirement is satisfied by either alone; two definitions is how the F7 four-definitions drift starts.

findings.finding: Q-DP-4 specifies the family-token gate in the EXCLUSIVE form that pass-2 rev-2 explicitly rejected, and the envelope field names disagree. Q-DP-4: 'Pass 2 DP-3's grep, extended to the queue layer: grep -nE "claude|deepseek|ollama|qwen|glm|minimax|kimi|gemma|\bpi\b" over the dispatch, resolution, appetite, and condition regions — excluding the data-table region delimited by pinned sentinel comments'. Pass-2 rev-2 F5 rejected exactly this shape: 'Rev 1 specified an exclusive gate (grep the file, minus the data tables). That inverts the form that shipped and works', and DP-3 now uses the INCLUSIVE sentinel-selected awk form (selection between /^\/\/ ── supervise: dispatch\/input region/ and /^\/\/ ── end supervise dispatch\/input/, comment-stripped). Also the decode-seam field is named stdout_envelope ∈ {raw, json_result} in S03 §11/Q-DP-2 but output_format ∈ {text, json-envelope} in pass-2 §3.1/DP-5 — the same capability, two vocabularies, and pass-2's DP-5 arms D2/D3/D4 are keyed to its names. Q-DP-1's placement ('pass 2 DP-2's canonical_models[] region in src/managent/main.zig, extended') agrees with pass-2 DP-2 in substance; the gate form and the field names do not.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Adopt pass-2 DP-3's inclusive sentinel form for the queue layer (select the region between the pinned sentinels, strip comments, grep — with the non-empty-selection loud-fail D1-empty carries), and rename stdout_envelope/json_result to output_format/{text, json-envelope} (or explicitly rule the rename and update pass-2's D2/D3/D4 keying). The two documents must build one gate.

findings.finding: Q-APP-3's reserved_for vocabulary cannot match the row field it gates. §11 says task_type is 'one of the 8 measured types' (the methodology §1 shares: audit, infra, battery, implement, orchestration, integration, research, spec). Q-APP-3's reserved_for = [deep-holistic-review, gate-holder-verification, spec-design-adjudication] and Q-APP-4(b)'s 'some SPEND family is qualified for the row's task_type (per docs/infra/model-task-matrix.md)' both assume a vocabulary that is neither the 8 measured types nor the matrix's T-A..T-H rows (model-task-matrix.md §2). A row whose task_type is constrained to the 8 types can never carry task_type = 'deep-holistic-review', so claude-fable's reservation admission (Q-APP-3: 'a row outside the list cannot resolve to a RESERVED family at all') is unsatisfiable as written — Fable becomes unreservedly undispatchable. The three taxonomies (8 measured types, T-A..T-H, the reservation prose) float without a mapping anywhere in the layer.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Pin one task_type taxonomy for the store field and express reserved_for (and the matrix's qualification predicate) in its vocabulary, or add an explicit mapping (e.g. reserved_for matches on a second tag field). Without it, the Q-APP-3 admission test and Q-APP-4(b) substitution rule are unbuildable and unverifiable.

findings.finding: Internal inconsistency in the per-tick enumeration cost: §2.1 Q-ORD-8(a) says 'at 12 eligible rows and a 10-second tick that is 24 file reads and 12 process spawns every 10 seconds' (2 bundle reads + 1 `managent show` spawn per eligible row — priority_of opens once, waiting_of opens once, added_of forks once; verified against fleet-keeper.sh:211-223, :229-258), while §10 change 3's 'why' column says '36 file reads + 18 subprocesses per tick today'. 36/18 is 3×/1.5× the row count and appears nowhere derivable from the code; §14's rejected-alternatives row repeats '36 files + 18 subprocesses'. One of the two numbers is wrong and the spec should carry one figure.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Pick the §2.1 figure (24 reads + 12 spawns at 12 eligible rows; note the uncounted 24 bundle globs — has_bundle, and the bundle_path calls inside priority_of/waiting_of) and correct §10 and §14 to match, or re-derive both from the code at build time.

findings.finding: src/managent/main.zig citations have no pinned commit and no longer resolve on disk. S03 pins fleet-keeper.sh citations to 1b8e627 (verified: the file is unchanged 1b8e627..HEAD, so every :211-258, :628-701, :721-782 citation resolves at both) but states no pin for main.zig, and its main.zig numbers (TaskState :66-107, canonical_models :115-126, `managent models` :334-337/:5161-5190, needsMet :1550-1557, deriveStatus :1559-1563) resolve exactly at 56b9cf1 (verified: TaskState at :66, canonical_models at :115, needsMet at :1550, deriveStatus at :1559, cmdModels at :5167 — S03 was authored against the pass-2-era tree) but not at HEAD (188154f): T569's d9d0331 shifted the file, so the same symbols now sit at :106, :155, :1590, :1599, :5207 and the models-verb dispatch at :375. Pass-2's own F11 discipline ('A citation that no longer resolves at 56b9cf1 is a spec defect') is the house rule; S03 adopted it for one file and not the other.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Add a citation-pinning header to S03 identical in form to pass-2's F11 (every file:line pinned to one commit, dirty files named). Given S03's main.zig numbers match 56b9cf1 exactly, 56b9cf1 is the natural pin; the numbers are stale at HEAD by ~40 lines and will keep drifting.

findings.finding: The cited pattern for the clock-free arms points at the wrong arm. §9: 'the clock-dependent arms seed a stale timestamp, exactly as the recovered regression-fleet-keeper.sh arm g seeds a 61-minute-old waiting_since (tools/regression-fleet-keeper.sh:890-929 is the pattern to copy for the ordering arms)'. Arm g is at :761-830 ('g. seeded: logjam flag after FLEET_LOGJAM_FLAG minutes', verified at 56b9cf1 and HEAD; the 61-minute seeds are at :774 and :803); :890-929 is arm h (waiting=1 bump). The substance is right (arm g does seed a 61-minute-old waiting_since); the range is wrong and a copying reader lands in the wrong arm.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Correct the range to :761-830 (or cite the seed lines :774/:803).

findings.finding: Two pass-2 section citations are rev-1 numbers that rev-2's insertion of §4/§5 shifted, and the pass-2 changelog's stability claim is incomplete. S03 §0 and §10 cite 'Pass 2 §8.2' for the behaviour-preserving fleet-fill statement; pass-2 has no §8.2 — the statement is §10.2 item 2 ('The fleet-fill loop is behaviour-preserving, not a redesign'; the §2.1 opening 'carried from tools/fleet-keeper.sh with no behaviour invention' is the other home). S03 §5.1 V7 cites 'pass 2 §4' for the ollama-stop release; pass-2 §4 is the appetite dial — the release is §6. Both were correct against pass-2 rev-1 and both drifted. The pass-2 changelog says 'S03-queue-layer/spec.md cites this document's §2.1, §2.5 and §3; all three keep their numbers' — true but incomplete: S03 also cites §8.2 and §4, which did not keep theirs.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Correct §8.2 → §10.2 and 'pass 2 §4' (V7) → 'pass 2 §6' in S03. Add a line to the pass-2 changelog noting the two additional S03 citations it did not enumerate.

findings.finding: D036 is cited without a timestamp and the directives file carries two D036 records. S03 §1.1 R9 attributes the durable default DENY = 'glm-5.2,minimax-m3,kimi-k2.7' to 'D036'. docs/infra/managent/directives.jsonl holds two D036 lines: 2026-08-04T23:46:36Z (target T361, an unrelated session-kill directive) and 2026-08-20T12:18:47Z (target T536, 'Ollama weekly tokens exhausted... ship FLEET_MODEL_DENY=glm-5.2,minimax-m3,kimi-k2.7 as a DURABLE default'). The intended record resolves by content but the file has no id uniqueness — the same pattern as D022/D023, which S03 does disambiguate by timestamp. The directives store's duplicated ids are a data defect in their own right (T574-era note; every id D021-D054 appears twice).
findings.disposition: ACCEPT (note). Timestamp the D036 citation in S03 (2026-08-20T12:18:47Z) the way D022/D023 are timestamped. The duplicate-id state of directives.jsonl is a separate data-integrity item for the kanban owner, not a spec defect.

findings.finding: Q-COND-5's live-store measurement has drifted since its 2026-08-21 snapshot, and one row has since gained an acceptance — the 'parks the entire dispatchable queue' consequence is directionally intact but the numbers have moved. The spec measured 18 dispatchable, 12 T-non-duty, zero with acceptance (T511, T522, T524, T525, T526, T527, T529, T530, T531, T533, T544, T548). At HEAD the store holds 254 rows: 21 dispatchable, 15 T-non-duty, 14 without acceptance — T573 now carries an acceptance command, and T571/T572 are new acceptance-less rows. The 9 done-but-not-passed rows still split 7 blocked / 2 abandoned (verified: ORCHA-FLASH, T541, T439, T349, T351, T358, T387, T361, T379), and T535 still needs T541 with T541 closed verdict=blocked — the Q-COND-2b live instance is current. _sys.closes is 94 (spec says 'currently 90'). The spec's own dates the measurement, so this is expected drift, not an error — but the §10 change-6 backfill precondition ('a named backfill row closed before the queue goes live') must be re-measured at build time, not against the spec's table.
findings.disposition: NOTE (re-measure at build). Q-COND-5's sizing paragraph should carry a 're-measure at build' marker, since its whole argument ('enforcing this condition as stated parks the entire dispatchable queue') is the load-bearing reason the change needs the backfill ruling.
